newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Disney wrong to sing Dalai's praises.
newsitem.headline: China says Disney wrong to sing Dalai's praises.

text.p: China said on Tuesday that Walt Disney Co would be wrong to sing the praises of Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama.

"To sing the praises of the Dalai Lama -- this kind of action does not conform with reality," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai said when asked to comment on Disney's backing for a Martin Scorsese film about the life of the Dalai Lama.
Cui accused the Dalai Lama of being the former "political and religious ruler of a feudal serf society... (and trying to) split the motherland under the cloak of religion".
"This kind of action...is wrong. Of course it does not enjoy popular support," Cui said of any praise for Tibet's god-king.
"We hope relevant parties could deal with this problem appropriately," he told a news briefing, without naming Disney.
The spokesman did not say if Disney's involvement in the film "Kundun" would hurt its business plans in China.
The Burbank, California-based entertainment giant is eager to expand into Asia, particularly China, where demand for U.S. products is high.
The Chinese Ministry of Radio, Film and Television declined to comment on reports that China had warned Disney. A ministry official said the matter was being studied.
Beijing has blamed the Dalai Lama for unrest in the Himalayan region and moved to root out his influence there.
The Dalai Lama won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989 for his non-violent campaign for autonomy for his homeland. He fled into exile in India in 1959 after an abortive uprising against communist rule.
